sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the appellant/insurer under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act challenging the liability fixed on the insurance company passed in MVC No.1182/2014 dated 09.08.2021 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC., at Tiptur (for short hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal').
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondents.
3. The ranks of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.
4. Previously the case was filed by the injured- claimant before the Tribunal.
Subsequently, during the pendency of the petition, he died.
The legal heirs were brought on record.

The case of the claimant before the Tribunal is that on 22.09.2013 at about 08.30 p.m., when the deceased Shadakshari T.C was proceeding in a motorcycle as a pillion rider and his father was riding the NC:
2024:KHC:27647 said motorcycle towards Bannihalli-Kallhalli Road, Tiptur Taluk, at that time, an Auto Rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-44-4608 driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motorcycle.

Due to which, the injured Shadakshari T.C fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he was taken to the Government Hospital, Tiptur and treated as in patient and taken treatment at Nimhans Hospital, Bengaluru and Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru and various Hospitals and he has filed the claim petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-.
During the pendency of the petition, the petitioner/injured died on 29.05.2015.
Hence, legal heirs were brought on record.

5. The insurer has filed objection to the claim petition prior to the death of the deceased and on taking various contentions, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the LR's petitioner prove that the deceased has sustained grievous injuries in the accident took place on 22.09.2013 at about 08.30 p.m., on Bannihalli-Kallhalli Road, Tiptur Taluk, NC: 2024:KHC:27647 was due to rash and negligent driving of Bajaj Auto vehicle bearing registration No.KA-44-4608 by its driver?
2. Whether the LR's petitioner are entitled for any compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?
3.
What award or order?
6. To prove the case, the petitioner No.1(a) was examined as P.W.1 and got marked 18 documents.
The respondent No.2 has examined R.W.1 and 5 documents were marked and R.W.2 was also examined and one document was marked at Ex.R.6.

7. After hearing the arguments, Tribunal has allowed the claim petition in-part by awarding compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum by the impugned judgment, which is under challenge.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellant-Insurer has contended that the claimant/deceased had died during the pendency of the petition and he was also insured with the NC: 2024:KHC:27647 ESI and getting ESI benefit.

Therefore, there is a bar for claiming any damages or claims under Section 53 of the Employees State Insurance Act 1948 and further contended that as per the Judgment of this Court, except the medical expenses or medical bills, the claimants are not entitled for any other compensation.
Hence, it is contended that the Tribunal without any medical bills has awarded Rs.2,00,000/- as a lump sum compensation, which is not correct.
Hence, prays for setting aside the same.

9. Per-contra, learned counsel for the respondents submitted that there are no documents available for production of the same, though they have spent medical expenses but they have not secured the medical bills etc.
Hence, prays for dismissing the appeal.

10. Having heard the arguments, perused the records, the points that arise for consideration is:-
NC: 2024:KHC:27647 1.
Whether the Tribunal justified in awarding Rs.2,00,000/- towards the medical expenses, inspite of no documents or medical bills produced?
2. Whether the claimants are entitled for any compensation in view of the bar under Section 53 of the ESI Act 1948?
11. On perusal of the records, it is not in dispute that the accident dated 22.09.2013 occurred due to the negligence driving of the driver of the Auto rickshaw.
However, the claimant himself filed the petition before the Tribunal for claiming compensation for the injures sustained by him in the accident.

But during the pendency of the claim petition, he died on 29.05.2015.
12.
It is not the case that the death was occurred due to the accident sustained in the road traffic accident.
There is no nexus between the death and the injury sustained by the claimant.
Such being the case, the legal heirs of the claimant are entitled only for the medical NC: 2024:KHC:27647 expenses, if they are incurred by them, when the injured was in the hospital.

13. Admittedly, the death had occurred after almost more than one and half years and it is not the case of the claimants that deceased died due to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled only for medical expenses.

14. Admittedly, the claimants have not filed any single document or any medical bills before the Tribunal and marked it or otherwise the claimant/deceased was insured as an employee under the ESI Act.
15. In view of the judgment passed by this Court in the case of Kannamma -vs-Deputy General Manager reported in ILR 1990 KAR 4300 Full Bench.

sentences.text: There is a bar under Section 53 of the ESI Act.
Such being the case, the question of granting compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- by the Tribunal without NC: 2024:KHC:27647 any records is not sustainable under the law.
Therefore, I am of the view that the appeal filed by the appellant- insurer deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, I pass the following:-
ORDER 1. Appeal is allowed.
2. The award of Rs.2,00,000/- awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No. 1182/2014 dated 09.08.2021 by the Court of the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC., at Tiptur is hereby set aside.
3. The claim petition filed by the deceased claimant represented by the legal heirs is hereby dismissed.
4. Amount in deposit is directed to be refunded to the appellant.
Sd/-
